title: China-to-Myanmar EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: AC Charging Connector and Site Socket Practice
rows.target_requirement: Myanmar does not publish an EU-style EV connector mandate for public AC charging. Type G domestic sockets based on BS 1363 are widely used in buildings, while EVSE connector acceptance is normally handled through project specification, MSTRD conformity documentation, installer review, and the local utility or site owner. A China GB/T AC connector should not be assumed acceptable without site-level confirmation.
target_standards: BS 1363 Type G socket practice in Myanmar buildings
MS/IEC 61851 where adopted or specified by project
rows.china_equivalent: China AC charging normally follows GB/T 20234.2 for the AC coupler and GB/T 18487.1 for the conductive charging system, with CPCNEC safety documentation and CCC baseline where applicable.
rows.gap: The gap is practical acceptance rather than a national Type 2 or CCS mandate. A GB/T AC outlet may be unfamiliar to Myanmar users and installers, and a Type G building supply point is not an EV charging connector. Exporters should specify the EV coupler, upstream socket or hardwire method, earthing, current rating, and signage for the specific site.

mandatory_status.target: No confirmed horizontal EV connector mandate; site and project acceptance required
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory China domestic baseline for GB/T EV charging interfaces where in scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat the connector choice as a site-specific Myanmar acceptance item. Do not market a China GB/T AC outlet as automatically compliant for Myanmar buildings or public use.

source.publisher: Ministry of Science and Technology, Myanmar

rows.target_requirement: Myanmar has no confirmed national rule requiring CCS2, CHAdeMO, or China GB/T for DC fast charging. DC connector selection is normally driven by the imported vehicle fleet, project tender, site operator, MSTRD conformity file, and utility acceptance. Chinese GB/T DC hardware should be treated as a compatibility choice, not a default Myanmar legal requirement.
target_standards: MS/IEC 61851 for conductive charging where adopted or specified
rows.china_equivalent: China DC charging commonly uses GB/T 20234.3 for the DC coupler, GB/T 18487 for the charging system, and GB/T 27930 for charger to BMS communication, with CPCNEC safety documentation and CCC baseline where applicable.
rows.gap: The main risk is fleet mismatch. A GB/T DC charger may suit China-origin vehicles but may not serve imported CCS or CHAdeMO vehicles without additional connector variants and communication support. Project documents should state the connector mix and supported vehicle communication protocols.

mandatory_status.target: No confirmed national connector mandate; project and fleet compatibility determine acceptance
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory China domestic baseline for GB/T DC charging interfaces where in scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm the Myanmar project fleet before shipping DC hardware. GB/T DC is not a substitute for multi-standard support where the site expects CCS or CHAdeMO vehicles.

source.publisher: Ministry of Science and Technology, Myanmar

rows.requirement: Connector Labelling, User Instructions, and Adapter Control
rows.target_requirement: For Myanmar deployment, connector markings and user instructions should identify the connector type, voltage, current rating, earthing arrangement, vehicle compatibility, and any adapter prohibition. Because connector practice is project-specific, clear English and Burmese or locally accepted instructions may be requested by importers, site owners, or installers.
rows.china_equivalent: China documentation normally labels GB/T 20234 connector type, GB/T 18487 charging mode, electrical ratings, warnings, and CCC or other certification marks where applicable.
rows.gap: China-only labels may not explain Myanmar site compatibility or safe adapter limits. If a product includes GB/T, CCS, CHAdeMO, or Type G-related supply accessories, the Myanmar file should separate EV couplers from building plugs and include local current and earthing limits.

mandatory_status.target: Usually project or importer requirement; mandatory where requested by permit, inspection, or installation acceptance
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory marking and instruction expectations under China product safety and certification practice where in scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Add Myanmar-facing connector labels and instructions before shipment. China-only GB/T labelling is unlikely to be enough for field acceptance.

source.publisher: Ministry of Science and Technology, Myanmar

rows.target_requirement: Myanmar does not operate an EU CE EMC regime for EV chargers. EMC evidence may still be requested in an MSTRD conformity file, import review, utility review, or project tender, especially for high-power DC chargers and equipment installed near communications or sensitive electrical systems. MS/IEC or IEC 61851 and IEC 61000 evidence is a practical route where requested.
rows.china_equivalent: China EV charger EMC evidence commonly references GB/T 18487.2, GB 17625.1, GB 17799.4, GB 4824, and CCC or CPCNEC supporting files where applicable.
rows.gap: Chinese EMC reports may be useful evidence but should be mapped to the IEC or MS/IEC standards requested by the Myanmar buyer, utility, or MSTRD reviewer. The gap is not CE marking; it is whether the file is understandable and acceptable for Myanmar review.

mandatory_status.target: Not confirmed as a horizontal EV charger EMC certification; may be required by MSTRD, utility, importer, or project
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory or certification-linked for China domestic market where in scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Prepare an IEC-mapped EMC dossier for Myanmar even though there is no EU-style CE EMC marking route. China GB reports alone may need explanation and cross-reference.

source.publisher: Ministry of Science and Technology, Myanmar

rows.target_requirement: Smart chargers with cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, RFID, or other radio functions may require Myanmar Post and Telecommunications related radio or telecom equipment approval before import or operation. The radio module, frequency band, power level, SIM or network use, and importer details should be checked before shipment.
target_standards: MPT radio or telecom equipment approval practice
rows.china_equivalent: China smart chargers may use SRRC-approved radio modules, China network access documentation, GB/T 27930 communication evidence, and CCC or CPCNEC baseline files where applicable.
china_standards: SRRC radio approval where applicable in China
rows.gap: Chinese SRRC or domestic radio approvals do not automatically authorize radio operation in Myanmar. A charger with removable or embedded radio modules should be reviewed module by module for MPT acceptance, permitted bands, and local operator requirements.

mandatory_status.target: Potentially mandatory for radio-enabled chargers before import or operation
mandatory_status.cn: China radio approval applies domestically where wireless modules are in scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] High attention item for smart chargers. Confirm MPT radio acceptance before shipping connected EVSE with cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or RFID functions.

rows.target_requirement: Myanmar Standards and Testing Research Division under MoST is the main standards and testing body. Standards are largely voluntary, but regulated or tendered categories can require conformity documentation, test reports, product specifications, labels, and importer declarations. EV chargers should be prepared with an IEC or MS/IEC mapped file for MSTRD or buyer review.
rows.china_equivalent: China domestic files typically include GB/T 18487, GB/T 20234, GB/T 27930 where applicable, CPCNEC safety materials, and CCC baseline certificates or test reports where in scope.
rows.gap: China GB documents should be converted into a Myanmar review dossier that explains IEC equivalence, deviations, rated voltage, grid conditions, connector choice, safety protections, and installation requirements. Do not assume CCC or CPCNEC documents are automatically accepted.

mandatory_status.target: Standards largely voluntary; conformity documentation may be required for regulated categories, import review, tenders, or utility acceptance
mandatory_status.cn: CCC and China standards apply domestically where in scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Build a Myanmar-facing MSTRD dossier rather than shipping only China certificates. The standards route is often voluntary, but documentation can still be a market-access gate.

source.publisher: Ministry of Science and Technology, Myanmar

rows.requirement: MIC Commercial Import Permit and Investment Interface
rows.target_requirement: Commercial import of EV chargers into Myanmar may require importer registration, MIC or related import permit handling, customs documentation, invoice, packing list, HS classification, and project approvals where an investment project or charging network is involved. The importer should confirm whether the shipment is normal trade, project import, or investment-linked import.
target_standards: Myanmar Investment Commission import and investment permit practice
Importer registration and commercial licensing practice
rows.china_equivalent: China export files usually include commercial invoice, packing list, export declaration, product certificates, GB/T and CCC documentation where applicable, and manufacturer test reports.
rows.gap: China export paperwork does not replace Myanmar import permission. The importer must align HS code, permit route, project status, and port route before shipment, especially for Yangon, Thilawa, or Mandalay overland entry.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where import permit, project approval, or customs licensing applies
mandatory_status.cn: China export clearance applies before departure but does not satisfy Myanmar import permission

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm MIC or related import-permit handling before shipment. Customs clearance risk is separate from technical conformity risk.

source.publisher: Directorate of Investment and Company Administration, Myanmar

rows.requirement: Customs Route, Port Entry, and Documentation
rows.target_requirement: EV charger shipments commonly enter Myanmar through Yangon or Thilawa seaport routes, with Mandalay relevant for overland logistics. Customs review may require correct HS classification, import licence evidence, conformity documents, invoice, packing list, bill of lading or waybill, and importer tax or company records.
target_standards: Myanmar Customs Department import documentation practice
Yangon and Thilawa seaport customs procedures
Mandalay overland logistics and customs practice
rows.china_equivalent: China-side paperwork covers export declaration, invoice, packing list, certificate package, and logistics documents, but usually does not determine Myanmar HS treatment or import licence status.
rows.gap: The Myanmar importer should pre-clear the HS code and permit packet before cargo departure. A technically acceptable charger can still be delayed if import licence, tax, or customs descriptions do not match.

mandatory_status.cn: China export customs clearance is separate and only covers departure from China

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat customs routing as a separate workstream. Yangon, Thilawa, and Mandalay routes should each be checked for paperwork and broker requirements.

rows.target_requirement: Myanmar does not have a confirmed horizontal RoHS regime equivalent to the EU RoHS Directive for EV chargers. Environmental, battery, packaging, hazardous-substance, or waste requirements may still appear in project specifications, tender terms, or sectoral rules, but they should not be described as a national horizontal RoHS requirement unless confirmed.
target_standards: No confirmed horizontal Myanmar RoHS equivalent for EV chargers
rows.china_equivalent: China products may include China RoHS marking or supplier material declarations in addition to GB/T 18487, GB/T 20234, CPCNEC safety, and CCC baseline documents.
rows.gap: Do not copy EU RoHS logic into the Myanmar target column. The honest position is that Myanmar lacks a confirmed horizontal RoHS requirement for EV chargers, while buyers may still request material declarations contractually.

mandatory_status.target: No confirmed horizontal RoHS mandate for EV chargers; contractual or project environmental requirements may apply
mandatory_status.cn: China RoHS may apply domestically depending on product classification and marking obligations

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Myanmar should be mapped as no confirmed horizontal RoHS for EV chargers. Provide material declarations only where the importer, tender, or buyer asks for them.

source.publisher: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Conservation, Myanmar

rows.requirement: Residual Current and Electric Shock Protection
rows.target_requirement: Myanmar EV charger installations should provide shock protection, leakage protection, protective earthing, overcurrent protection, and safe isolation suitable for the site supply. MSTRD, MEPE, ESE, project engineers, or installers may ask for IEC 61851 and IEC 60364 evidence, especially for public or commercial sites.
target_standards: MEPE or ESE site acceptance requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China EV chargers commonly rely on GB/T 18487 leakage and safety requirements, GB/T 20234 connector safety, CPCNEC safety documentation, and CCC baseline testing where applicable.
rows.gap: A China protection design may be technically sound but still needs Myanmar site documentation. The file should state RCD or RDC-DD strategy, earthing assumptions, isolation monitoring for DC chargers, upstream breaker sizing, and installer responsibilities.

mandatory_status.target: Required as part of safe installation and utility or project acceptance, even if no separate national EVSE protection certificate is confirmed
mandatory_status.cn: China domestic safety and certification expectations apply where in scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Provide a Myanmar installation protection schedule. Do not rely on a China safety report without explaining the protection architecture for the local site.

rows.target_requirement: Outdoor EV chargers in Myanmar should be designed for local weather, lightning exposure, earthing quality, surge protection, enclosure IP rating, heat, humidity, and grid disturbances. Project engineers or utilities may require surge protective devices and site-specific earthing or lightning protection measures.
target_standards: IEC 61643 surge protective device practice where specified
MEPE or ESE site acceptance requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China chargers may include surge protection, IP rating, temperature rating, and GB/T 18487 or CPCNEC safety evidence, but these are often documented for China site assumptions.
rows.gap: Myanmar outdoor deployment may demand stronger site adaptation than the China baseline. Exporters should document SPD type, upstream protection, earthing resistance assumptions, enclosure rating, thermal derating, and maintenance inspection intervals.

mandatory_status.target: Project and utility acceptance item; mandatory where specified by site design, tender, or electrical inspection
mandatory_status.cn: China domestic protection design applies to China installations and does not automatically settle Myanmar site protection

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Outdoor Myanmar installations should include a local surge, earthing, IP, and thermal design check. Treat this as a site engineering requirement, not just a product certificate item.

rows.requirement: EV Charger Product Safety and IEC 61851 Evidence
rows.target_requirement: Myanmar standards are largely voluntary, but EV charger product safety files should be prepared around MS/IEC 61851 or IEC 61851 where adopted, specified, or requested. MSTRD, buyers, utilities, or project owners may ask for test reports covering electric shock protection, insulation, temperature rise, charging control, interlocks, enclosure protection, and markings.
rows.china_equivalent: China product safety evidence usually references GB/T 18487, GB/T 20234 connector standards, CPCNEC safety files, and CCC baseline testing where applicable.
rows.gap: A China GB/T test report should be mapped to IEC 61851 clauses and Myanmar project requirements. Differences in connector assumptions, rated voltage, installation environment, marking language, and protection devices should be called out.

mandatory_status.target: Standards largely voluntary; safety evidence may be mandatory through MSTRD, import review, tender, utility, or installer acceptance
mandatory_status.cn: China domestic safety and CCC baseline apply where in scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Prepare an IEC 61851 mapped safety file for Myanmar review. China GB/T evidence is useful but should not be presented as automatically sufficient.

source.publisher: Ministry of Science and Technology, Myanmar

rows.requirement: Grid Voltage, Frequency, and Power Quality
rows.target_requirement: Myanmar nominal supply is 230 V, 50 Hz. The 50 Hz frequency matches China, but the nominal voltage differs from China's common 220 V single-phase and 380 V three-phase assumptions. For commercial AC and DC chargers, MEPE, ESE, the site owner, or the project engineer should confirm service capacity, phase arrangement, transformer capacity, voltage tolerance, harmonics, and load management.
rows.china_equivalent: China chargers are commonly designed and tested around 220 V single-phase and 380 V three-phase 50 Hz supply assumptions under GB/T 18487 and related grid or installation practice.
china_standards: China 220 V and 380 V 50 Hz supply assumptions
rows.gap: Frequency adaptation is usually low risk because both markets use 50 Hz. Voltage and site capacity are the real gaps. Datasheets should confirm operation at 230 V nominal, input voltage range, derating, phase balance, harmonic mitigation, and restart behavior under unstable supply.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for grid connection and field acceptance by utility, site owner, or project engineer
mandatory_status.cn: China domestic voltage assumptions apply domestically but must be rechecked for Myanmar

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm 230 V 50 Hz and local capacity before shipment. Same frequency as China does not remove the need for Myanmar voltage and grid checks.

rows.target_requirement: Myanmar commercial EV charger projects should include installation drawings, single-line diagrams, load calculations, earthing design, protection settings, commissioning checklist, and utility or site acceptance records. MEPE or ESE involvement may be needed depending on location, capacity, and grid connection type.
rows.china_equivalent: China installation packages may include GB/T 18487 installation assumptions, GB/T 51313 or GB 50966 style infrastructure design documents, CPCNEC safety evidence, and CCC baseline files where applicable.
rows.gap: China installation templates should be converted to Myanmar site drawings and utility documents. Capacity, transformer interface, earthing, protection coordination, fire access, civil works, and maintenance responsibility should be resolved locally.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for commercial field installation acceptance where utility, project owner, or inspector requires it
mandatory_status.cn: China domestic installation documents do not substitute for Myanmar site acceptance

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat installation acceptance as a Myanmar engineering deliverable. Product certification alone will not settle site energization.

rows.requirement: Smart Charging Back Office, OCPP, and Payment Integration
rows.target_requirement: Myanmar does not have a confirmed AFIR-style public charging rule mandating ad-hoc payment, OCPP, or ISO 15118. Smart charging requirements are usually set by the project owner, charge-point operator, payment provider, mobile network provider, or utility. OCPP support, local payment integration, offline operation, and remote monitoring should be specified contractually.
target_standards: Project owner or charge-point operator requirements
ISO 15118 where specified by vehicle or project requirement
rows.china_equivalent: China smart chargers commonly support GB/T 27930 for DC vehicle communication, domestic operator platforms, QR payment flows, and GB/T 34658 interoperability evidence, alongside GB/T 18487 and GB/T 20234 baseline documents.
rows.gap: A China cloud or payment stack may not work in Myanmar because of SIM, payment, language, data hosting, and support constraints. The exporter should confirm OCPP version, local SIM or Ethernet support, Myanmar payment gateway integration, offline charging behavior, and maintenance access.

mandatory_status.target: Not confirmed as national mandate; mandatory where specified by operator, payment provider, tender, or utility project
mandatory_status.cn: China domestic protocols and platform requirements apply only to China deployments

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Smart charging should be specified as a Myanmar project integration item. Do not assume a China operator cloud or payment flow is usable without local testing.

rows.target_requirement: Connected EV chargers in Myanmar should define data flows, remote access, firmware update control, user account handling, payment data handling, and incident response. Requirements may come from the site owner, telecom provider, payment provider, or public-sector procurement terms rather than a single EVSE-specific cybersecurity rule.
target_standards: Telecom provider requirements where connected services are used
Payment provider requirements where payment data is processed
rows.china_equivalent: China products may include domestic cybersecurity, platform, app, QR payment, and firmware update controls tied to China cloud services and GB/T 27930 or operator protocols.
rows.gap: Myanmar deployment may require a different cloud region, local administrator access, English or Burmese interfaces, payment data controls, and local service arrangements. The exporter should avoid hard dependencies on China-only servers, China-only SIMs, or China-only payment accounts.

mandatory_status.target: Project or contract requirement unless a separate telecom, payment, or public procurement rule applies
mandatory_status.cn: China domestic platform controls do not automatically satisfy Myanmar operation

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Review connected charger data and remote-operation design before Myanmar rollout. Local SIM, cloud, payment, and support dependencies are often the practical blocker.
